notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1989:A.2.30.3 AR1 defines cs as "the string of one or more characters specified by argument-2", and §1989:A.2.30.3 AR4 asks only that argument-2 be "a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item". The compiler applies §2023:15.68.3 AR2's content bans at every edition ("Argument-2 shall not contain any of the digits 0 through 9", the characters * + - , . and the letter pairs CR and DB): BindNumvalCFamily refuses such a literal argument-2 with COBOL1627, and the runtime InvalidCurrency makes NumvalCDec return 0 for such a data item. So at --std 85 a currency string such as "CRC" or "Rs." is refused or yields 0 where argument-1 has the 1989 format. The rest of the rule conforms: the Verified row's class and category screen refuses numeric, alphabetic and edited argument-1, and NvScan accepts both 1989 formats (leading sign before cs, trailing + - CR DB, comma groups, ".75"). The row's change record does not list this 2023 restriction. The witness uses the currency string "$".

next.reason: The two content formats (spaces, sign, currency string, digits with grouping and decimal separators, trailing +/-/CR/DB) match §2023:15.68.3 AR4, and §2023:15.68.3 AR2 restates cs as argument-2's currency string. But 1989 allows only 'a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item' with uppercase CR/DB, while 2023 allows 'category alphanumeric or national' (§2023:15.68.3 AR1) and CR/DB 'in uppercase or lowercase' (§2023:15.68.3 AR4), plus a LOCALE form (§2023:15.68.3 AR5). Looser.
